episodes.summary: Blue Owl reported its third quarter yesterday. It's the first alternative-manager result this desk has had in hand this season. And it moves something we've tracked all week into a manager's own reported numbers. The money raised for private credit is now outrunning the money actually lent.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — October 30, 2026
episodes.summary: We lead with a deal that extends the question we asked yesterday: who is still writing checks now that sponsors have largely stopped buying from each other. On Thursday, October 29th, Thrive Holdings agreed to take ADT private. That makes it the second time the home-security company has gone private in a decade.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — October 30, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's headline: Amazon confirmed the hyperscaler cash squeeze is an industry story, and the market sorted the spenders by earnings delivery, punishing Amazon and Alphabet for misses and rewarding Microsoft for a beat.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — October 30, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the scorecard. One call resolved, and it comes with a correction I owe you.

episodes.title: Frontier AI Lab Competition — October 31, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's the thesis. This week the market got its first hard scoreboard for a frontier lab's unit economics. But the same week also showed what that scoreboard can't see: procurement trust and the hidden cost of containment.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — October 31, 2026
episodes.summary: Yesterday this desk said that outside mega-cap tech, the alarm wasn't ringing. We also said that if earnings damage spread, the hedges that had just run off would get re-bought at a higher price. On Friday, the alarm rang. So the question this morning isn't whether markets sold off. They did.

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — October 31, 2026
episodes.summary: Yesterday we closed on an open question. When a hack hits the most liquid offshore exchange, do holders of the regulated Bitcoin ETFs de-risk alongside everyone on that exchange? Or does the wrapper insulate them, the way its design promises?

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — October 31, 2026
episodes.summary: This week the pattern across minerals, fuel, chips, and money is the same. The deadlines are arriving before the capacity.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — October 31, 2026
episodes.summary: Two threads this desk has been pulling on all week came together within forty-eight hours. They turn out to be the same thread. On Tuesday we argued that PC and device buyers, unlike compute-constrained accelerator buyers, would have to eat the cost of the HBM boom.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — October 31, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's throughline is simple. AI agents are getting cheaper and more heavily used faster than they're getting trustworthy. We'll take it in three steps. First, a number about the risk. Second, a rollout this month that shows what the controls look like inside a shipping product. Third, a number about the reward.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — October 31, 2026
episodes.summary: On Friday, this show concluded that the demand question at the infrastructure layer was settled for now. It was three hyperscalers out of three, with Microsoft, Amazon, and Google Cloud all showing backlog growing faster than revenue. The filings and calls since then ask a harder question.

episodes.title: AI in Biopharma R&D — October 31, 2026
episodes.summary: The headline this week is a consolidation, not a launch. Flagship Pioneering has folded three of its own AI-discovery biotechs into a single new company called Etcelera. Cellarity, Etiome, and Empress Therapeutics no longer exist as separate entities. They're now one platform, run by CEO Ad Rawcliffe.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — October 31, 2026
episodes.summary: This week's firmest commitments in physical AI didn't go to humanoids. They went to factories and warehouses. Today we'll look at two deals. Waymo is handing its next robotaxi to a Toyota assembly plant. And Walmart has locked a multi-billion-dollar automation commitment into an SEC filing.

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — October 31, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's story is that SpaceX's lead has turned into a dependency, and that dependency gets priced two different ways. Militaries treat it as a vulnerability. Bond markets treat it as a reason to lend cheap.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — October 31, 2026
episodes.summary: The headline this week is a split screen. The liquidity scare in private credit is easing. The credit stress underneath it just printed a record. That isn't a contradiction.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — October 31, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the largest deal in play this week, and start with the caveat: these are talks, not a deal. The Financial Times reported on Friday that Clayton, Dubilier and Rice is working with GTCR on a joint take-private bid for Global Payments.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — October 31, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's headline: Friday's two shocks, Intel's guidance collapse and the record Binance hack, look idiosyncratic rather than systemic, but they hit hard because the Fed has left markets with no policy cushion.
